Content:
When a radical equation contains two square roots, like

Content:
[MATH: \sqrt{2-x} - \sqrt{x} = 0,]

Content:
we manipulate the equation so that we have one square root on each side:

Content:
[MATH: \sqrt{2-x} = \sqrt{x}.]

Content:
Then, we raise both sides to the power of [MATH: 2,] and we solve the equation as usual:

Content:
[MATH: (sqrt(2 − x))^{2}|= (sqrt(x))^{2}; 2 − x|= x; 2x|= 2; x|= 1]

Content:
Finally, we check whether the obtained value [MATH: x=1] is actually a solution of the original equation:

Content:
[MATH: sqrt(2 − (1))|= ^(?)sqrt((1)); sqrt(1)|= ^(?)sqrt(1); 1|= 1✓]

Content:
Therefore, the only solution of [MATH: \sqrt{2-x} - \sqrt{x} = 0] is [MATH: x=1.]

sections.normalized_html:
First, we move the radicals to separate sides of the equation:

[MATH: sqrt(2x + 5) − sqrt(x + 6)|= 1; sqrt(2x + 5)|= sqrt(x + 6) + 1]

Then, we raise both sides to the power of [MATH: 2\mathbin{:}]

[MATH: sqrt(2x + 5)|= sqrt(x + 6) + 1; (sqrt(2x + 5))^{2}|= (sqrt(x + 6) + 1)^{2}; 2x + 5|= (sqrt(x + 6))^{2} + 2sqrt(x + 6) + 1^{2}; 2x + 5|= x + 7 + 2sqrt(x + 6); 2sqrt(x + 6)|= 2x + 5 − x − 7; 2sqrt(x + 6)|= x − 2]

Now we have an equation with one square root on one side and a linear expression on the other side. To solve this type of equation, we raise both sides to the power of [MATH: 2] one more time:

[MATH: (2sqrt(x + 6))^{2}|= (x − 2)^{2}; 4(x + 6)|= x^{2} − 4x + 4; 4x + 24|= x^{2} − 4x + 4; x^{2} − 8x − 20|= 0; x^{2} − 10x + 2x − 20|= 0; (x − 10)(x + 2)|= 0; x = 10, − 2]

Finally, we check the obtained values by substituting them into the original equation.

  • Checking [MATH: x=10,] we get [MATH: sqrt(2(10) + 5)|= ^(?)sqrt((10) + 6) + 1; sqrt(25)|= ^(?)sqrt(16) + 1; 5|= ^(?)4 + 1; 5|= 5.✓] So, the value [MATH: x=10] is indeed a solution of the original equation

  • Checking [MATH: x=-2,] we get [MATH: sqrt(2(− 2) + 5)|= ^(?)sqrt((− 2) + 6) + 1; sqrt(1) = 1|≠ 2 + 1 = 3.×] The value [MATH: x=-2] does not satisfy the original equation, so we discard it.

Therefore, the equation [MATH: \sqrt {2x +5} -\sqrt {x+6} = 1] has a single solution [MATH: x=10.]
